# Front speaker replacement and fitment

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Replace front 6.5" component speakers by removing door panels, unhooking harnesses, and adapting cones. [t1858]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Remove the door panel by taking out trim pieces, screws around the handle, and clips behind the side mirror.
2. Unplug any window or lock switch harnesses from the back of the door panel.
3. Lift the entire door panel away from the metal frame to unhook it from the base of the window sill.

_Procedure reported by [t1858]._

## Tools

- Phillips screwdriver [t1858]
- Trim removal tool (implied by 'pry') [t1858]
- Razor blade [t1858]
- Pliers or needle-nose pliers [t1858]

## Parts

- [Partial] 6.5" Component speakers [t1858]
- Trim screws with wide flange [t1858]

## Tips & gotchas

- [Partial] Use shallow depth speakers to prevent the rear from hitting the window glass when rolled down. [t1858]
- [Partial] Gut the stock speaker cone and use its plastic ring as a spacer adapter for better fitment. [t1858]
